facts.statement: Agilisaurus is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived in eastern Asia during the Middle Jurassic Period.
facts.quote: Agilisaurus (; 'agile lizard') is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic Period of what is now eastern Asia.

facts.statement: The only known species is Agilisaurus louderbacki, found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: The only named species is A. louderbacki, recovered from the Lower Shaximiao Formation of Sichuan, China.

facts.statement: Agilisaurus grew to be approximately 1.2 to 1.7 meters long, 60 centimeters tall at the hip, and weighed around 40 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was about 1.2-1.7 m in length, 60 cm in hip height, and 40 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Agilisaurus possessed leaf-shaped teeth adapted for an abrasive, plant-based diet.
facts.quote: It has leaf-shaped teeth that were well-adapted to its abrasive, plant-based diet.

facts.statement: Agilisaurus had wavy tooth enamel previously thought to be unique to hadrosaurs, suggesting it was more resistant to wear.
facts.quote: Most surprisingly, the wavy enamel of the teeth of this genus (and all other ornithopods), presumed to make them more resistant to wear, was previously thought to be exclusive to hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: The only known specimen, the holotype, was discovered in 1984 during the construction of the Zigong Dinosaur Museum.
facts.quote: The holotype, which is the only known specimen, was discovered in 1984, during the construction of the Zigong Dinosaur Museum.

facts.statement: The genus and species were named by Peng Guangzhou in 1990 and described in detail in 1992.
facts.quote: Both genus and type species were named by Chinese paleontologist Peng Guangzhou in very brief fashion in 1990, then described in further detail by Peng in 1992.

facts.statement: With a tibia measuring 20.7 cm and a femur measuring 19.9 cm, Agilisaurus was likely an extremely fast bipedal runner that used its tail for balance, though it may have walked on all fours while feeding.
facts.quote: Its tibia (lower leg bone), at 20.7 cm in length, was slightly longer than its femur (upper leg bone), at 19.9 cm in length, which indicates that it was an extremely fast bipedal runner, using its long tail for balance, although it may have walked on all fours when browsing for food.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists suggest Agilisaurus may have been a burrow dweller because it lacked tail-stiffening bony struts.
facts.quote: Because it lacks tail-stiffening interwoven bony struts, some paleontologists think it may have been a burrow dweller.

facts.statement: Agilisaurus was originally classified in the family Fabrosauridae, a group no longer considered valid by most paleontologists.
facts.quote: It was originally placed in the family Fabrosauridae, which is no longer considered valid by most paleontologists.

facts.statement: One recent analysis places Agilisaurus basal to heterodontosaurs on the branch leading to Marginocephalia.
facts.quote: In one recent cladistic analysis, Agilisaurus was found in a position basal to heterodontosaurs in the branch leading to Marginocephalia.

facts.statement: Peng initially assigned the species formerly known as Yandusaurus multidens to the genus Agilisaurus as Agilisaurus multidens in 1992.
facts.quote: In his more thorough 1992 description, Peng added a new species to the genus Agilisaurus. This species had previously been known as Yandusaurus multidens. Because this species did not belong in the genus Yandusaurus and due to similarities with A. louderbacki, it was assigned the name Agilisaurus multidens.

facts.statement: In 2005, the species was reassigned to its own genus, Hexinlusaurus, due to disagreement over its placement in Agilisaurus or Yandusaurus.
facts.quote: Other scientists were not convinced that this species belonged to either Yandusaurus or Agilisaurus, and in 2005, it was once again reassigned, this time to its own newly created genus. It is now known as Hexinlusaurus multidens.

facts.statement: Peng described a second species of Agilisaurus in 1992.
facts.quote: En su descripción de 1992, Peng se refiere a una segunda especie de Agilisaurus.

facts.statement: This species was previously known by the name Yandusaurus multidens.
facts.quote: Esta especie es conocida anteriormente bajo el nombre de Yandusaurus multidens.

facts.statement: Peng assigned the name Agilisaurus multidens because the species did not belong to Yandusaurus and showed similarities with A. louderbacki.
facts.quote: Debido a que esta especie no pertenecía a Yandusaurus y a las similitudes con A. louderbacki, le asignó el nombre de Agilisaurus multidens.

facts.statement: Other scientists were unconvinced that the species belonged to Yandusaurus or Agilisaurus, leading to its reassignment in 2005 to its own newly created genus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo otros científicos no estaban convencidos de que esta especie hubiese pertenecido a Yandusaurus o Agilisaurus, y en 2005, fue reasignado de nuevo, esta vez a su propio género creado recientemente.

facts.statement: The species is now known as Hexinlusaurus multidens.
facts.quote: Ahora se conoce como Hexinlusaurus multidens.

facts.statement: Multiple studies agree that this species is slightly more derived than Agilisaurus.
facts.quote: Varios estudios convienen que esta especie es levemente más derivada que Agilisaurus.

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Bajocian to the Oxfordian, between 170.9 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Oxfordian (170.9 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus is Neornithischia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Neornithischia

facts.statement: The genus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
